comment: M13 (user decision, Oct 28): class periods play as cutscenes, not walking: the bell and the walk to class, then the class itself with the teacher at the board and a seating chart of who's in it. Lines use {class}, {teacher}, {room}, {period}, {mate}. Art ids (art_class_<class id>) are optional; a dark backdrop stands in.
walkLines: The bell. Lockers slam, sneakers squeak, and the hall empties toward {room}.
Between periods the hall is a river. You let it carry you to {room}.
Someone's phone plays the same ten seconds of a song. You follow the noise to {room}.
You take the long way past the trophy case. Nobody's polished it since the nineties. {room}, then.
classLines: {teacher} is already writing on the board when you slip in. {class}, period {period}.
{teacher} looks up, counts heads, and starts without waiting. {class}.
The radiator clanks. {teacher} talks over it like it's a student. {class}, period {period}.
mateLines: {mate} is doodling on the desk again.

stage.comment: Class periods as real scenes (user request, Oct 29): the walk is the school hall interior with you walking across it; the class is the room's interior with the teacher at the board and everyone in a seat behind a desk. rooms maps a class's room to an interior in data/town/interiors.json; seatKinds are furniture you sit behind; hallStudents is how many students loiter in the hall.
